assessment.nobel_worthiness: Very high. The China-shock research and the task-based account of technology changed how economists and policymakers understand trade adjustment, local labour markets and wage polarisation. It combines credible empirical design with a clear conceptual framework, and it has had large influence across labour, trade and political economy.
assessment.attribution: The local labour-market effects of import competition are most cleanly credited to Autor, Dorn and Hanson. The task-based framework has a wider authorship, including Lawrence F. Katz and others outside this list. Choosing three names leaves out Katz, which is a real attribution cost.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The core papers date from about 2013 to 2016 and have been replicated, extended and debated for a decade. The long-run persistence results are well documented.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to credit the task framework over the trade-shock evidence, which would change the laureate set.
Continuing debate about the magnitude and external validity of the China-shock estimates.
Overlap with the Katz credit in other ballot entries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Very high. Firm heterogeneity and selection reshaped trade theory and empirics after the new trade theory. They explain exporter premia, reallocation gains and the extensive margin, and they underpin much of modern quantitative trade analysis and policy work.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central theoretical contribution. Helpman, with co-authors such as Melitz and Yeaple, extended it to FDI and to trade-flow estimation. Redding is credited for quantitative and spatial extensions and is a plausible third name, but the two-name core is cleaner. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum have important empirical precursors that are not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with more than twenty years of confirmation. The framework is widely used and its empirical predictions have been tested in firm-level data.
uncertainties: Credit for the empirical precursors on exporter heterogeneity outside the credited names.
Helpman may also be considered under the separate trade-politics ballot entry.
Whether a third laureate should be added.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High. Random-coefficients demand estimation with endogenous prices, together with dynamic industry models, made empirical analysis of differentiated-product markets practical. It is now standard in merger review, antitrust and regulatory work, and it connects economic theory to data with real policy consequences.
assessment.attribution: Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes (the BLP estimator) are the clearest core. Pakes's work on dynamic games (Ericson-Pakes) and on estimation adds to his case. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are significant but secondary or more specialised. A three-name selection is defensible but excludes some important figures.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The methods date from the 1990s and are widely adopted, with extensive replication and refinement.
uncertainties: Credit allocation between BLP and other structural IO pioneers such as Bresnahan.
Concern that structural estimates are sensitive to modelling assumptions.
Uncertainty about whether the committee treats this as econometrics or industrial organisation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High. Foundations of International Macroeconomics put open-economy macro on intertemporal, microfounded footing. The 'redux' model and the exchange-rate disconnect work (Meese-Rogoff, the Obstfeld-Rogoff puzzles) identified lasting problems. Their influence on policy analysis is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff are the natural pair for the intertemporal framework and the puzzles. Credit for disconnect and pass-through evidence is shared with a wider empirical literature. Rogoff also appears in a separate crisis-history entry.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with about thirty years of influence. The puzzles remain only partly resolved, which is a scientific caveat rather than an absence of impact.
uncertainties: Whether unresolved puzzles count as achieved discovery rather than agenda-setting.
Competing credit for New Open Economy Macroeconomics and for pricing-to-market and invoicing-currency research.
Overlap between Rogoff's two ballot entries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High. Staggered nominal contracts and the New Keynesian framework are the basis of modern monetary policy analysis and central-bank models. Their influence on theory and practice is very large, and they build on microfoundations of price setting.
assessment.attribution: Calvo (1983) and Taylor (1980) supply the staggered-price mechanisms, and Woodford supplies the policy framework. Galí, Gertler, Christiano and Eichenbaum, and Smets, are also strongly credited, so any three-name selection is contestable. The field is a broad collective achievement.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The framework has been used for decades and tested through the financial crisis and the post-pandemic inflation, with ongoing challenges.
uncertainties: High attribution ambiguity among at least eight credited names.
Empirical criticism of Calvo-style pricing, given the evidence on menu costs and asymmetric adjustment.
Overlap with earlier macroeconomics prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High. Kiyotaki-Moore's model of credit cycles shows how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks. It underlies much of the macro-finance and financial-friction literature, including work after 2008.
assessment.attribution: The 1997 paper is a clear two-person contribution. Gertler and Gilchrist are credited for the financial accelerator and its empirical work, but Bernanke's 2022 prize already acknowledged part of that line. A two-name selection is cleaner for attribution.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with confirmation from the 2008 crisis and subsequent empirical and quantitative work.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize.
Possible need to include Gertler.
Mostly theoretical contribution, with indirect empirical validation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Moderately high to high. Mian and Sufi showed with granular data that household leverage drove the housing boom, the consumption collapse and the depth of the recession. The work is influential in macro-finance and policy.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are the clear pair for the household-debt evidence. Campbell is credited on the list for household finance and mortgage work but is a less natural fit for this specific discovery.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature, with roughly fifteen years of citation and replication. Some debate remains over mechanisms and over the generality of the credit-supply view.
uncertainties: Debate over identification and the generality of the findings.
Relatively recent compared with other candidates.
Whether the committee sees this as a discovery or as an application of existing frameworks.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Moderately high. Population administrative data established new facts on intergenerational mobility, geographic variation and neighbourhood effects, with substantial policy and methodological influence. The scale and creativity of the empirical programme are notable.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the main driver across the programme. Hendren is central to the mobility and neighbourhood work. Friedman and Katz are co-authors on several key papers, so any selection leaves out co-credited names. Chetty also appears on the public-economics entry.
assessment.maturity: Less mature than the other candidates. The central findings date from about 2014 onward, and long-run validation of causal neighbourhood effects is still developing.
uncertainties: Possible premature timing for causal interpretations.
Attribution within a large collaborative team.
Overlap with the public economics ballot entry and Chetty's other prize-relevant work.
